name: goodwill
quote: I'll give him the benefit of the doubt.
description: A willingness to show someone trust or kindness when you don't have a good reason to be nice to them.

variations.name: perceived goodwill
variations.description: A perception that someone is showing another kindness. Your reaction may range from admiration to contempt depending on the context and your outlook.

comparisons.description: Having goodwill towards people doesn't have to blindly assume the optimistic best case. You might be aware that they might not 'do the right thing', but that treating them positively has a chance of encouraging pro-social behavior.
Goodwill doesn't necessarily involve being generous with time or materials - it can just be trust, kindness, and encouraging words.
Trusting a stranger with something important may involve faith in human nature.

variations.name: goodwill mindset
variations.description: A pattern of belief that people react well to assuming their intentions are unselfish.

variations.name: account of goodwill
variations.description: We may keep an internal tally of how much a person or group has earned or spent our positivity towards them.

commentaries.quote: We unconciously balance a 'trust account' for every person and social group. At a certain level of trust, we'll treat that person or group well and assume they have good intentions. If your bar of trust is so high that you assume only a few people are trustworthy, you're protecting yourself in pretty cynical way. If your bar of trust is at the 'extended friends and family' level, you're normal. If your bar of trust is at the 'stranger' level, you're practicing goodwill. Finally, if you can can assume positive intentions about someone even when you expect them to respond poorly, you are probably benevolent and enlightened.

You should be wary when your goodwill account with someone is getting low. If you get to a trust level of zero, the best case is that your benefactor walks away. There are many worse cases, some of them quite unpleasant. This goes whether you're a person, a company, a government, or a species.
Goodwill is the one and only asset that competition cannot undersell or destroy.

conditions: A willingness to show a person or group trust or kindness when you don't have a good reason to be nice to them.
